# Fixture repository and oracles

Status: carried over from the 2026-10-07 plan, change oracles and the sibling fixture added 2026-10-14, regression guards added 2026-10-14 (#13) · the week, still-here and change oracles run as `go test` in `internal/app` (`TestWeekOracle`, `TestStillHereOracle`, `TestChangeOracles`, `TestDeterminism`, #13), web escaping in M3

`internal/fixture` builds this repository (`fixture.Main`), the [sibling fixture](#sibling-fixture) (`fixture.Sibling`) and the [regression guards](#regression-guards-testchangeoracles)' two repositories (`fixture.Backdated`, `fixture.MergedRevert`) in temporary directories for `go test`. Every number below is an oracle: a change that moves one fails CI. Each oracle exists so that one specific wrong implementation fails, and that implementation is named next to it.

CI runs real git; porcelain output is never faked. The `GitRunner` port exists so git flags live in one place, not so tests can avoid running git.

## Setup

- **Dates.** `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE` and `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE` are 12:00:00Z on the stated day. The 2026-10-06 commits use the times in the table instead, so their order is stable.
- **Window.** `--now 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z`, so the default week starts at `2026-09-30T00:00:00Z`. No commit sits on that boundary.
- **Blank lines.** Every week insertion except Frank's `spaced.py` is a non-blank line. The blank inside `service.py` was committed in January, so it is a still-here fact, not a week fact.
- **Mailmap.** The repo config sets `log.mailmap=false`. The test passes this file with `--mailmap`:

```
Ada Example <ada@example.com> <ada@other.example>
```

- **Deny list.** The deny list used in M0 includes patterns that deny `go.sum`, a `vendor` segment, and the two consecutive segments `bootstrap/cache`. `gen_out.py` is denied by the header sniff, not by a path pattern.

## Measured blame

Measured on 2026-10-08 with Git 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155). The repository for that run contained only these `app.py` and `service.py` commits, plus a work-tree `.mailmap` with the Ada line above. Sibling files in the real fixture change the commit SHAs, but not which author owns each line. `git blame -w -M -e service.py` printed:

```
^e9db5aa app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 1) def beta_stable_block():
^e9db5aa app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 2)     return "beta stable block here"
^e9db5aa app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 3) def alpha_moved_block():
^e9db5aa app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 4)
^e9db5aa app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-01 12:00:00 +0000 5)     return "alpha moved block kept"
2c7a4b6b app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-02 12:00:00 +0000 6) def gamma_added_later():
2c7a4b6b app.py     (<ada@example.com> 2026-01-02 12:00:00 +0000 7)     return "gamma added by second mail"
d720564f service.py (<bob@example.com> 2026-10-06 13:00:00 +0000 8) def delta_bob_added():
d720564f service.py (<bob@example.com> 2026-10-06 13:00:00 +0000 9)     return "delta added on the branch"
```

Gamma's author header was `ada@other.example`, and the mailmap rewrote `author-mail` to `ada@example.com` before counting. Non-blank lines in the file: Ada 6 (beta 2, alpha 2, gamma 2), Bob 2 (delta). Ada is the majority owner (`6/8 >= 0.5`); Bob is not.

`--line-porcelain` emitted four groups, of sizes 2, 3, 2 and 2:

- Beta is the first size-2 group.
- Alpha is the size-3 group. It is separate from beta even though both lines belong to the init commit, because blame starts a new group when the original line numbers are not contiguous (`4 1 2`, then `1 3 3`).
- The blank line is the middle content line of the size-3 group. Its record repeats the author headers, has no fourth field, and its content is a single tab.

The init SHA in that isolated run is `e9db5aab2e60fc152a91b4249739fcb8d0c7cfc2`:


`--porcelain` (not `--line-porcelain`) on the same file printed the beta continuation line as `e9db5aab2e60fc152a91b4249739fcb8d0c7cfc2 5 2`, followed by the tab-prefixed content, with no second `author` line. CI runs `--line-porcelain`; the parser still accepts the suppressed form ([blame-collector.md](../../docs/spec/blame-collector.md#porcelain-parsing)).

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **Group-size multiplier.** It scores the size-3 group as 3 and the file as Ada 7 / Bob 2. The tab-line counter scores that group as 2, giving Ada 6 / Bob 2.
- **Four-field-only matcher.** It drops alpha's blank line and its `return` line.
- **Missing `-M`.** Beta goes to Bob's reorder commit and alpha stays with Ada. The file becomes Ada 4 / Bob 4, both are majority owners, and the 6/2 oracle fails. Note that dropping `-M` moves the block that moved up, which is beta.
- **Blocks too short.** The previous draft's short lines (`def alpha():`, a blank, `return 1`, `def beta():`, `return 2`) are 15 and 14 alphanumeric characters. On the same git, `-w -M` gave the same result as running without `-M`, so those lines are not the fixture.

## Week oracle (M0, `TestWeekOracle`)

`lines_added` counts numstat insertions, blank lines included, on any path that received a role. `prod_lines_added` is the `prod` subset. Assert the set of rows: the display order (`lines_added` descending, then email ascending) is not a rank.

| Who | Email | Commits | lines_added | prod_lines_added |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bob Builder | `bob@example.com` | 2 | 11 | 11 |
| Ivy Tester | `ivy@example.com` | 1 | 4 | 0 |
| Frank & Sons | `frank@example.com` | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| Ada Example | `ada@example.com` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Dana Dev | `dana@example.com` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Erin Editor | `erin@example.com` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Jules Note | `jules@example.com` | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| GitHub Copilot (bot table) | `copilot@bot.example` | 1 | 3 | 3 |

Why each row is what it is:

- **Bob, 11.** The merge's first-parent diff adds `side.py` (2) and `side_week.py` (7), which is 9. It does not add `main_only.py`, which is already on the first parent. Delta adds 2.
  - `--no-merges` drops the merge and keeps Cara's October commit, so Cara appears and Bob's 11 becomes 2.
  - `-m` alone changes nothing on 2.50.1: under `--first-parent` it still yields the first-parent diff, so Bob stays 11. Dropping `--first-parent` as well diffs the merge against its second parent too, which adds `main_only.py`'s 5 lines, so Bob becomes 16, and the walk reaches Cara's October commit, so Cara appears with 7.
- **Cara absent.** Her February commit is outside the window, and her October commit is not on the first-parent walk; its 7 lines are part of Bob's merge diff. Gina and Hank are absent too.
- **Erin, 1.** With default rename detection, her row is 1 insertion and 0 deletions on `new_name.py`. `--no-renames` would record a full-file add. Storing the raw `old_name.py => new_name.py` string would fail classification.
- **Frank, 3.** Numstat counts 3 insertions, but only 2 of his lines are non-blank. A week counter that skips blanks fails here. Frank's still-here count is 2.
- **Ivy, 4 and 0.** `tests/test_service.py` matches the segment pattern `(^|/)tests(/|$)`, but the substring `/tests/` does not occur in it. `notes.csv` is unclassified and adds 0, yet the commit still counts.
- **Jules, 0.** A commit that touches only an unclassified path still makes a row.
- **One Ada row.** Her in-window commit is authored as `ada@other.example` while `log.mailmap=false`. `%aN`/`%aE` give one row at `ada@example.com`; `%an`/`%ae` would give a second row.
- **`--days 1`.** Against `[week].days = 7`, the report writes `window.days` 1, `days_from` `cli`, and `since` `2026-10-06T00:00:00Z`; an override the report ignores leaves `window.days` at 7. `history`, the window the run collected, equals `window`, as in every week report ([report-json.md](../../docs/spec/report-json.md#shape)): an override that reaches the report but not the collector leaves `history` at `[2026-09-30, 2026-10-07)`. The rows do not move: every week landing is on 2026-10-06, inside both windows.

## Still-here oracle (M1, `TestStillHereOracle`)

The headline counts `prod` non-blank lines only.

| Who | prod_nonblank_lines | majority_files | Bot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ada Example | 10 (`service.py` 6, `new_name.py` 3, `ada_week.py` 1) | 3 | no |
| Cara Dev | 9 (`side.py` 2, `side_week.py` 7) | 2 | no |
| Bob Builder | 7 (`service.py` 2, `main_only.py` 5) | 1 (`main_only.py` only) | no |
| Frank & Sons | 2 | 1 (`spaced.py`) | no |
| Gina Split | 2 | 1 (`split.py`) | no |
| Hank Split | 2 | 1 (`split.py`) | no |
| Dana Dev | 1 | 1 (`kept.py`) | no |
| Erin Editor | 1 | 0 (`1/4` of `new_name.py`) | no |
| GitHub Copilot | 3 | 1 (`bot.py`) | yes |

- **`split.py` is a 2/2 split.** Gina and Hank each have `majority_files == 1`, and the file counts once. A reducer that uses only `max()` fails one of those two assertions. The prefix would still be Ada and Cara, which is why the assertion is on both authors rather than on the prefix.
- **The concentration walk.**
  - `files_with_majority` is 10: `service.py`, `new_name.py`, `ada_week.py`, `kept.py`, `spaced.py`, `split.py` (counted once), `side.py`, `side_week.py`, `main_only.py`, `bot.py`.
  - The sum of `majority_files` is 11. Half of 10 is 5.0.
  - Sorted by `majority_files`, then `prod_nonblank_lines`, then email: Ada (3, 10) brings the running sum to 3; Cara (2, 9) brings it to 5; stop.
  - `authors_in_prefix` = 2, `bots_in_prefix` = 0.
- **Excluded files.** No headline lines come from `tests/test_service.py`, `go.sum`, `vendor/lib.py`, `vendor/new.py`, `gen_out.py`, `bootstrap/cache/config.php`, `notes.csv` or `extra.csv`.
  - A segment check that compares one path component to `bootstrap/cache` leaves the PHP file in `prod`, and Ada's 10 becomes 14.
  - Dropping the mailmap splits the 3 lines Ada wrote as `ada@other.example` (gamma's 2 in January, `ada_week.py`'s 1 in October) into a second person, leaving 7 at `ada@example.com`, which fails her 10.

## Change oracles (M1, `TestChangeOracles`)

These values were derived by hand from the History table and the definitions in [metrics.md](../../docs/metrics.md#change-facts-shared-by-durable1-and-simplifying1), then confirmed with plain git 2.50.1: `log -p -U0 -w`, `blame -w -M --line-porcelain`, `rev-list L^1..L` and `log --grep`. The commands and their output are in the pull request for issue #3. No stillhere code produced any of them. An independent audit re-derived every value here and in the [sibling fixture](#sibling-fixture) from the definitions as amended on 2026-10-14, which credit blamed lines like commits, and re-ran the commands with plain git and through `gitcli.Runner`. It changed no number; its pull request holds the evidence.

With `--now 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z`, every window is half-open and starts and ends at 00:00:00Z:

| Window | Interval | Main fixture landings in it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `durable@1` cohort | `[2025-10-07, 2026-07-09)` | 7, from 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-01 |
| `simplifying@1` window and `who_knows@1` recent landers | `[2026-07-09, 2026-10-07)` | 9, all on 2026-10-06 |
| `knowledge_loss@1` activity | `[2026-04-10, 2026-10-07)` | the same 9 |

Assert values, not display order. Ratios are exact fractions; three decimals are shown for reading. Short commit IDs are for debugging; tests should not assert them.

### durable@1 (main fixture)

| Who | Σ surviving / Σ added | durable@1 | N | Ranked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ada Example | 9 / 9 (rows 1, 2) | 1.000 | 2 | no, below 10 |
| Bob Builder | 5 / 7 (rows 3, 7) | 0.714 | 2 | no |
| Gina Split | 2 / 2 | 1.000 | 1 | no |
| Hank Split | 2 / 2 | 1.000 | 1 | no |

No one else has a value.

- **Bob's move (row 3).** The `-U0 -w` patch keeps alpha and gamma where they are and re-adds beta at the top: 2 added, 2 removed. Blame `-M` credits beta's two lines to the init commit, so the move keeps 0 of its 2. By definition, a move inside one file scores 0 for the mover. That is open decision 6: `durable@2` would blame at the landing commit and leave the move out of `added`. Ada's init keeps all 7 of its lines.
- **Ada's rename (row 4).** With rename detection the patch has no content lines. It adds nothing, so it is not a cluster, and Ada's N is 2, not 3.
- **Cara has no value.** Both her commits landed with row 8 on 2026-10-06, inside 90 days, although `e08df80` was written on 2026-02-01. The cohort goes by landing time.
- **Merges.** Row 8 is outside the cohort, and no line at HEAD is blamed to a merge commit.
- **Blank lines.** Row 1 adds the blank inside alpha, and it counts in neither column.

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **Missing `-M` in blame.** Beta goes to the move: Ada 7/9 (0.778), Bob 7/7.
- **`--no-renames` in the patch.** Row 4 adds the 6 non-blank lines of `service.py` and keeps none: Ada 9/15 (0.600), with N 3.
- **Numstat instead of non-blank lines.** Row 1 adds 5 lines of `app.py`: Ada 9/10.
- **Roles or the deny list ignored.** Row 1 also adds the 2 lines of `tests/test_service.py`, or the 23 denied lines.
- **No mailmap.** `ada@other.example` becomes a second person with 2/2.
- **Commit time instead of landing time.** `e08df80` joins the cohort: Cara 2/2, with N 1.
- **N counts landings.** Ada's N becomes 3.

### knowledge_loss@1 (main fixture)

Per repository. The root is the only area that holds `prod` lines, so its value is the same.

| Surviving `prod` lines | Lines |
| --- | --- |
| Held by people: the still-here table without the bot | 34 |
| Whose credited person has a landing in `[2026-04-10, 2026-10-07)`: Ada 10, Cara 9, Bob 7, Frank 2, Dana 1, Erin 1 | 30 |
| Whose credited person has none: Gina 2 (last landing 2026-01-06), Hank 2 (2026-01-07) | 4 |
| **`knowledge_loss@1`** | **4 / 34 = 0.118** |

GitHub Copilot's 3 lines are credited to a bot, because its commit names no co-author, and are in neither count. No commit in the main fixture has a co-author, so here the credited person is always the blame author.

- **Cara is active** through the landing map: row 8 landed her commits on 2026-10-06. She has no first-parent landing of her own.
- **Ada is one person.** Her 2026-10-06 landing is authored as `ada@other.example`, and the mailmap folds it into the address that holds her 10 lines.

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **Landing authors only, without the landing map.** Cara looks gone: 13/34.
- **No mailmap.** `ada@example.com` holds 7 lines (`service.py` 4, `new_name.py` 3) and has no landing since 2026-01-05: 11/34.
- **The mailmap on blame but `%ae` on landings.** All 10 of Ada's lines look gone: 14/34.
- **Bots in the denominator.** 4/37 (0.108).

### who_knows@1 (main fixture)

| Path | Majority owners | Top surviving-line authors | Recent landers (90 days) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `service.py` | Ada (6 of 8 non-blank lines) | Ada 6, Bob 2 | Bob (row 9) |
| `split.py` | Gina and Hank (2 of 4 each) | Gina 2, Hank 2 | none: last landed 2026-01-07 |
| `side.py` | Cara (2 of 2) | Cara 2 | Cara (`e08df80`, landed by row 8) |

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **Missing `-M`.** `service.py` becomes Ada 4, Bob 4, with both as majority owners.
- **`max()` only.** `split.py` loses one of its two owners.
- **No window on landers.** Gina and Hank appear as recent landers of `split.py`.
- **Crediting the merger, or patching with `log --first-parent -p`.** Bob replaces Cara as the recent lander of `side.py`: with `--first-parent`, git gives row 8 its first-parent diff, which adds `side.py` and `side_week.py` as Bob's.
- **Commit time instead of landing time.** `side.py` has no recent lander, because `e08df80` was written in February.

### AI-assisted tags and reverts (main fixture)

There are none. No commit has a `Co-authored-by` trailer, so no landing is AI-assisted: the share is 0 of 16 landings. GitHub Copilot's 2026-10-06 commit names no human co-author, so it is a bot commit, not an AI-assisted one, and it stays in the bot table. The revert query returns nothing.

## Sibling fixture

`fixture.Sibling(t)` builds a second repository, named `sibling`, for the change cases that the main History must not hold. Those are AI-assisted trailers, reverts, a reformat listed in `.git-blame-ignore-revs`, a whitespace-only change, simplifying deletions, and enough landings to rank someone. A separate repository keeps the main oracles from moving.

### Sibling setup

- **Dates.** Every commit is at 12:00:00Z on the stated day, with the same author and committer. No commit is within a day of 2025-10-07, 2026-04-10, 2026-07-09, 2026-09-07 or 2026-09-30, so no window membership depends on how a boundary is treated.
- **Now.** `--now 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z`, the same as the main fixture. The windows are the ones in the table at the top of the [change oracles](#change-oracles-m1-testchangeoracles).
- **Mailmap.** The repo config sets `log.mailmap=false`. The test passes this file with `--mailmap`. It maps the GitHub noreply address in C1's trailer to Pia:

```
Pia Pair <pia@example.com> <81234567+piapair@users.noreply.github.com>
```

- **Content.** Where a row gives only a line count, the file holds lines `<name>_<i> = <i>`, and the subject is `feat: add <file>`. Every non-blank line is unique in the repository.
- **Commit IDs.** They are stable, because the build is hermetic and uses SHA-1: HEAD is `d8d9a79387bdaa6e9da6153a9c886c1a4bcfcdfd`. Here they are part of the content, because the revert messages and `.git-blame-ignore-revs` contain full commit IDs. Tests should still find a landing by its row (date and author), not by its SHA.

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **A case-sensitive trailer key.** L3 is missed. A case-sensitive `git log --grep='^Co-authored-by:'` lists four commits and not L3. Git's trailer parsing, `%(trailers:key=Co-authored-by)`, finds all five.
- **Matching the name.** Q1 is tagged because its co-author is named Claude.
- **Matching `noreply` loosely.** Q1 is tagged through its GitHub noreply address.
- **Reading only the landing commit's trailers.** M is not tagged.
- **Crediting C1's author.** C1 goes to Copilot in the bot table, and Pia's `durable@1` N drops to 1.
- **Co-authors not canonicalised.** C1 goes to `81234567+piapair@users.noreply.github.com`, a second person.
- **Crediting human co-authors.** Claude Dupont appears with Q1's 6 lines.

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **Grouping by the blame author.** Blame names C1's git author, so `retry.py`'s 4 lines go to Copilot in the bot table: Pia has 5, the bot share is 4 of 120, and Copilot becomes the majority owner of `retry.py`. `durable@1` still credits C1 to Pia, so the two metrics disagree about who wrote the same commit.
- **Co-authors not canonicalised.** The 4 lines go to `81234567+piapair@users.noreply.github.com`, a second person, and Pia has 5.
- **Crediting the first co-author whoever the author is.** L3, O4 and P2 give their lines to the agents in their trailers, and Q1 gives its 6 to Claude Dupont: Lena 34, Omar 33, Pia 7, Quinn 25.

## Regression guards (`TestChangeOracles`)

Two small repositories hold history shapes that once broke the history collector (the review of #37) and that neither fixture may hold, because each would move its oracles: `fixture.Backdated(t)` and `fixture.MergedRevert(t)`. Each is its own repository, so a guard that fails names its own cause.

- **Setup.** Each is scanned alone with `--now 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z`, no mailmap and the packaged policy, so the windows are those of the [change oracles](#change-oracles-m1-testchangeoracles). Every commit is at 12:00:00Z on the stated day, with the same author and committer except the backdated guard's A2, which was authored and committed on different days by different people; no date is within a day of a window boundary. Where a row gives only a line count, the file holds lines `<name>_<i> = <i>` and the subject is `feat: add <file>`. Commit IDs are stable, as in the sibling, and are for debugging only.
- **Derivation.** The values below were derived by hand from the History tables and [metrics.md](../../docs/metrics.md#change-facts-shared-by-durable1-and-simplifying1), then confirmed with plain git 2.50.1 through `gitcli.Runner` (`log --first-parent` with `--since` and with `--since-as-filter`, `rev-list M^1..M`, `log --no-walk --stdin --grep`, `blame -w -M`). The commands and their output are in the pull request for #13 that added them.

### Backdated first-parent commit (`fixture.Backdated`)

X is a first-parent commit whose committer date, 2025-06-01, is older than the scan's 365-day window, as `git rebase --committer-date-is-author-date` or a wrong clock leaves a commit. It sits above two landings in the window and below two more. The top one, A2, is the other way round: its author date, 2025-04-14, is older than the window and its committer date is inside it, as `git rebase`, `git cherry-pick` and GitHub's rebase merge leave a commit. Each keeps the author and the author date, and whoever replays the commit becomes its committer: Cal wrote A2, and Bea rebased it onto `main`.

| Row | When | Author | What | Commit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | 2026-02-02 | Bea Below `<bea@example.com>` | `bea.py` (4 lines), the root commit: a `durable@1` cohort landing | `0a28836` |
| B2 | 2026-08-03 | Cal Below `<cal@example.com>` | `cal.py` (2 lines): a 90-day window landing | `53dd3dd` |
| X | 2025-06-01 | Dot Dated `<dot@example.com>` | `dot.py` (1 line), committed on `main` on top of B2 | `d4fc72d` |
| S1 | 2026-08-10 | Cal | On `side`, branched from X: `side.py` (2 lines) | `dc041ab` |
| A1 | 2026-08-17 | Bea | `--no-ff` merge of `side`, `Merge branch 'side'`: a window landing above X | `8924a5a` |
| A2 | 2026-08-24, authored 2025-04-14 | Cal, committed by Bea | `rebased.py` (2 lines), on `main` on top of A1: a window landing by its committer time, written before the window | `d910bc4` |

The first-parent chain from HEAD is A2, A1, X, B2, B1. Landings are chosen and dated by committer time, so the landings in `[2025-10-07, 2026-10-07)` are B1, B2, A1 and A2: X's committer time is outside the window, so X is no landing and no landing's map holds it, while A2's is inside, whatever its author date. A1's map is {A1, S1}, and A2's is {A2}.

| Metric | Who | Value | N | Clusters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `durable@1` | Bea Below | 4 / 4 | 1 | B1 |
| `simplifying@1` | Cal Below | 0 removed, 0 simplifying landings | 3 | B2, S1 landed by A1, and A2 (at 2026-08-24) |

No one else has a value in either metric: Bea's A1 is a merge commit, which never counts; A2 is credited to its author, Cal, not to Bea, who committed it; and Dot has no landing.

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **Plain `--since`.** It stops the `--first-parent` walk at X, the first commit older than the window: `git log --first-parent --since=2025-10-07T00:00:00Z` prints A2 and A1 alone, where `--since-as-filter` prints A2, A1, B2 and B1. The history window then holds 2 landings instead of 4, Bea has no `durable@1` value, and Cal's `simplifying@1` N is 2.
- **A backdated commit's claim given to the landing above it.** The landing map is one walk for every landing ([week-collector.md](../../docs/spec/week-collector.md#landing--commit-map)). If only landings claimed commits, A1 would claim X, and Dot would get a `simplifying@1` cluster: 0 removed, N 1.
- **Choosing landings by author time** (`%at`, where the window is committer time). A2 is then no landing: the history window holds 3 landings, and Cal's `simplifying@1` N is 2.
- **Dating landings by author time** (`Landing.Time` from `%at`). A2 still lands, but at 2025-04-14, outside every metric's window: Cal's `simplifying@1` N is 2, with no cluster at 2026-08-24.
- **Crediting the committer** (`%cN`/`%cE` instead of `%aN`/`%aE`). A2 goes to Bea, who gets a `simplifying@1` cluster, 0 removed, N 1; Cal's N is 2.

### Revert merged with `--no-ff` (`fixture.MergedRevert`)

Each revert is made on a side branch and landed by a `--no-ff` merge whose message names no revert, as a pull request merged with GitHub's default merge method lands: only the commit the merge brought in says `This reverts commit <sha>.` ([week-collector.md](../../docs/spec/week-collector.md#subjects-and-reverts)). M1 lands a delete-then-revert in the `durable@1` cohort and M2 an add-then-revert in the 90-day window: the two ways an unseen revert earns credit ([metrics.md](../../docs/metrics.md#change-facts-shared-by-durable1-and-simplifying1)).

| Row | When | Author | What | Commit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| D1 | 2026-01-12 | Wes Reverted `<wes@example.com>` | `refactor: drop legacy_1 to legacy_4`: deletes the first 4 lines of `legacy.py` | `8753903` |
| R1 | 2026-01-19 | Rex Revert `<rex@example.com>` | On `undo-d1`, branched from D1: `git revert --no-edit` of D1, which restores the 4 lines | `2f389e3` |
| M1 | 2026-01-26 | Mia Merge `<mia@example.com>` | `--no-ff` merge of `undo-d1`, `Merge branch 'undo-d1'` | `575bf23` |
| N1 | 2026-02-09 | Nia | `nia.py` (3 lines) | `5e0bae3` |
| X2 | 2026-08-03 | Wes | `wes.py` (20 lines) | `eee85d8` |
| R2 | 2026-08-10 | Rex | On `undo-x2`, branched from X2: `git revert --no-edit` of X2, which deletes `wes.py` | `6965c0f` |
| M2 | 2026-08-17 | Mia | `--no-ff` merge of `undo-x2`, `Merge branch 'undo-x2'` | `e38d376` |
| N2 | 2026-08-24 | Nia | `nia_w.py` (1 line) | `82ed0c1` |

The landings in `[2025-10-07, 2026-10-07)` are D1, M1, N1, X2, M2 and N2. M1's map is {M1, R1}, and M2's is {M2, R2}. The revert query over the mapped commits returns two links:

| Revert landing | Its revert commit names | Reverted landing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 (2026-01-26) | `87539038da7cc3c8233f467504a1a7ea30ad5c3b` (R1) | D1 |
| M2 (2026-08-17) | `eee85d8e100c39f254183866fa0b19632e5c16c0` (R2) | X2 |

| Metric | Who | Value | N | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `durable@1` | Nia Normal | 3 / 3 | 1 | N1. D1 only deletes, so it is no cluster; M1 is a revert landing |
| `simplifying@1` | Nia Normal | 0 removed, 0 simplifying landings | 1 | N2. X2 is reverted, so every commit of it leaves; M2 is a revert landing |

Rex, Wes and Mia have no value in either metric. `surviving@1` excludes no commit, so it holds what blame `-w -M` gives each person at HEAD, 10 `prod` lines in all:

| Who | `surviving@1` | Blamed lines at HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nia Normal | 6 | `legacy_5` and `legacy_6` from U0, `nia.py` 3 (N1), `nia_w.py` 1 (N2) |
| Rex Revert | 4 | `legacy_1` to `legacy_4`, which R1 restored: blame credits restored lines to the revert, the blind spot `durable@1` names |

Wes holds no line, because D1 only deleted and R2 deleted `wes.py`; neither merge commit holds one, and no bot does.

Wrong implementations this catches:

- **Revert detection on the first-parent walk** (`git log --first-parent --grep`, which reads only the landings' own messages). It finds no revert here. M1 then credits Rex with R1's 4 restored lines, which blame gives to R1: `durable@1` 4/4, N 1. X2 stays in, so Wes has a `simplifying@1` cluster, 0 removed, N 1; and M2 credits Rex with R2's 20 removed lines: `simplifying@1` 20, N 1, with a simplifying landing (net −20).
- **Revert links at commit grain** (`Revert.SHA` set to the revert commit, not to the landing whose map holds it). R1 and R2 are no landings, so M1 and M2 are not revert landings: Rex has `durable@1` 4/4 and `simplifying@1` 20. D1 and X2 are still reverted, so Wes has no value.
- **Leaving a revert landing's commits out of `surviving@1`**, as the change metrics leave revert landings out. Rex then holds nothing, and the people's lines at HEAD sum to 6, not 10.

## Tests that are not extra commits in this history

Ada's oracle stays stable only if these cases stay out of the fixture repo.

- **Classify** (`TestClassify`):
  - `tests/test_service.py` gets role `test`, and `bootstrap/cache/config.php` is denied.
  - A faked size above `max_bytes` is `too_big`; do not commit a 400 KB blob.
  - Pin the precedence among path roles with `tests/fixtures/x.py` ([classification.md](../../docs/spec/classification.md#roles)).
- **Rename paths** (`TestNumstatRename`, a small repository built with `git fast-import`): the collector reads numstat with `-z` ([week-collector.md](../../docs/spec/week-collector.md#parsing)), so each form git would print without it gives the true destination and source, in week and scan runs alike. `dir/{old => new}/file.py` gives `dir/new/file.py`; `x/{y => }/z.py` gives `x/z.py`, not `x//z.py`; `a => b => c` gives `b => c` renamed from `a`, with no warning; a modified file named `{x => y}.py` keeps its name and is not a rename; quoted and octal-escaped names keep their own bytes. Scan runs add each file's non-blank lines from its own patch, so a blank line added in a rename counts in numstat only.
- **Policy** (`TestPolicy`):
  - A user file that omits `[bots]` exits 2 and names `bots`.
  - `policy.sha256` stays the hash of the file.
  - The deny list loads: a `generated_paths.txt` line that `regexp.Compile` rejects, such as a lookahead `(?=…)` (RE2 has none), fails the test. The real file's header names RE2, Linguist (MIT), and the upstream commit that was read. (This was `TestDenyListLoads`; it is part of `TestPolicy`.)
  - The `--days 1` override of `[week].days` is the [week oracle](#week-oracle-m0-testweekoracle)'s, in `TestWeekOracle`.
- **Attributes** (`TestAttributes`, a tiny second repo):
  - A packaged deny plus `-linguist-generated` is not denied.
  - No deny plus `linguist-generated` is denied.
  - A deny with one attribute unset and the other set stays denied.
  - Repeat all three against a bare clone of that repo; without `--source` every case would read `unspecified`.
- **Clone health** (`TestCloneHealth`):
  - A `--depth 1` clone warns `shallow-clone` and has no blame facts.
  - A `--filter=blob:none` clone warns `partial-clone`, and has commit facts but no line facts.
  - With a fake promisor URL, assert that nothing connects under the Analysis profile (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` and `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=none`). The 2.45 floor means the assertion is never skipped, and neither variable is ever unset.
- **Ignore-revs** (no test of its own: the [sibling](#sibling-fixture) oracles cover it, in `TestChangeOracles`): a root `.git-blame-ignore-revs` at the scanned SHA is used and recorded. Blame looks through F, so L5 keeps 3 of 3 in `durable@1`; F is no `simplifying@1` cluster; and the run records `blame_ignore_revs` with source `root` and F's full ID. `--ignore-revs-file` on a multi-repo run is a usage error ([report-json.md](../../docs/spec/report-json.md#exit-codes)) that no test asserts yet.
- **Prefix with odd M** (no test yet: [codebase.md](../../docs/spec/codebase.md#tests) lists none): three authors with `majority_files` 1 each, so M = 3 and half is 1.5, with equal lines on two of them. The walk stops at ≥ 1.5, and the email tie-break decides who the second author is.
- **Display name** (no test yet: [codebase.md](../../docs/spec/codebase.md#tests) lists none): one email, no mailmap name, two names with equal counts. The newer committer timestamp wins; equal timestamps fall through to UTF-8 bytes ascending.
- **Cache** (`TestCacheAmend`, only if open decision #3 is approved): blame the fixture, then amend a blamed commit away without `git gc`. `git cat-file -e` of the old HEAD still exits 0, and the next scan misses every blame fact.
- **Hotspots** (only with open decision #1):
  - Option A: with the jar absent, `hotspots.status = skipped`, `reason = jar-not-found`, and still-here rows are unchanged. CSV fixtures under `testdata/maat_csv/` cover an ambiguous display name and a path that no longer exists, with `ownership` as a 0–1 ratio and `degree` as an integer percent.
  - Option B: the tables equal a one-time code-maat run on this fixture.

Every address is in one repository (`local:fixture` or `local:sibling`), and the run's as-of time is `--now`, so the hand-off rule's earlier address must have no commit on or after 2026-07-09.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main fixture, no `--mailmap` | 11 | 1: `copilot@bot.example` | Ada (medium); Gina → Hank (low, a guess) |

The agents in L3, O4 and P2's trailers are bots, as Copilot is.

No address is shared and no group is left out as oversized, so `shared` and `oversized` are 0 in all four scans: every address's commits carry one author name, no local part is a role or default one, and no name is a default (the last words of Cara Dev, Dana Dev and Ivy Tester are generic, their first are not). `example.com` is the main domain of both fixtures: 10 of the main fixture's 11 people use it, and 5 of the sibling's 7, whose other two are GitHub noreply addresses.

### Wrong implementations this catches

- **Co-authors not read.** The two noreply addresses and the agents appear only in trailers: the sibling has 5 addresses and 1 bot, and Pia's candidate is gone.
- **Blamed commits older than the history not read.** Uma disappears: the sibling has 6 addresses without its mailmap, 5 with it.
- **Bots and agents kept.** The main fixture has 12 and 11 addresses, the sibling 10 and 9.
- **A local part made from the name counted as a second rule.** Ada becomes high, and her line is written uncommented: one signal, the name, counted twice.
- **A name alone written as a line** (a medium candidate not commented out). The printed mailmap maps `ada@other.example` to Ada and `81234567+piapair@users.noreply.github.com` to Pia unread, where the facts cannot tell either pair from two people of one name.
- **The newest address as canonical** outside a hand-off. Ada's line becomes `# Ada Example <ada@other.example> <ada@example.com>`, not `MailmapText`.
- **A hand-off suggested as certain** (medium or high, or its line uncommented). The printed mailmap maps `gina@example.com` to Hank Split and merges two people.
- **A hand-off without the shared file.** Gina then has two successors within 30 days (Hank and Cara) and Cara two predecessors (Gina and Hank), so the ambiguity rule keeps none: Gina → Hank disappears.
- **A hand-off without the quiet period.** With the mailmap, Ada, whose last commit is on 2026-10-06 at 18:00, hands off to Ivy, whose first is an hour later in `tests/test_service.py`, which Ada's init created: a person still at work, read as one who left.

### The TestChangeOracles row (for the integrator, #13)

The [issue](https://github.com/IHaveASegway/stillhere/issues/26) adds no test of its own; this is the row `TestChangeOracles` gains. Scan each fixture into a fresh facts.db, once without its mailmap and once with it, and call `app.Identities` with the zero scope. Assert `addresses` and `bots` from the first table, `shared` and `oversized` 0, and each candidate's confidence, guess and commented flags (`commented` is true for all three), rules, suggested name, canonical address and addresses (email, name, domain kind, commits, co-authored, first, last, repos) from the tables above; Ada's `same-local-part` link has `from_name` true; for Gina → Hank, a gap of 24 hours and one shared file, `split.py`. Then write `report.Mailmap`'s output for the scans without a mailmap to a file. It holds the three lines `# Ada Example <ada@example.com> <ada@other.example>`, `# Hank Split <hank@example.com> <gina@example.com>` and `# Pia Pair <pia@example.com> <81234567+piapair@users.noreply.github.com>`, and no line that is not a comment. Run `git check-mailmap` in each fixture through `gitcli.Runner` with that file as `Config.MailmapFile`: `<ada@other.example>`, `<81234567+piapair@users.noreply.github.com>` and `<gina@example.com>` all come back unchanged, since adding the output unread merges nobody. With the `# ` removed from those three lines, `<ada@other.example>` gives `Ada Example <ada@example.com>`, `<81234567+piapair@users.noreply.github.com>` gives `Pia Pair <pia@example.com>`, and `<gina@example.com>` gives `Hank Split <hank@example.com>`.

## Discovery fixture (`TestDiscover`)

Two clones whose `origin` is `https://user:TOKENVALUE@github.com/example/widget.git`, plus a third clone with a different remote:

- The run keeps one widget and skips the other with `duplicate-repo`. The warning names the two local paths and `https://github.com/example/widget.git`, and nothing else.
- `TOKENVALUE` appears nowhere in stdout, stderr, the JSON output, or (from M1) the facts store.
- A bare repository given as `PATH`, and a bare child of a group, are scanned rather than skipped; their branch comes from `symbolic-ref HEAD`.
- A work-tree clone and a bare mirror with the same HTTPS remote are duplicates.
- `git@github.com:o/r.git` and `https://github.com/o/r.git` stay two separate repos.

`fixture.Discovery` builds the layout. Every repo is a clone of one upstream whose `main` has two commits and whose `trunk` is one commit ahead of `main`; a clone's `origin` is the URL named below, or absent. Each row is one `Discover` call, and the expected result follows from the layout and [discovery.md](../../docs/spec/discovery.md), not from the code:

| Paths named | Repos (key) | Groups | Warnings and failures | Wrong implementation it catches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `widget-b`, `other`, `widget-a` | `https://github.com/example/other.git`; `https://github.com/example/widget.git` at `widget-a` | | `duplicate-repo`: `skipped <widget-b>; same remote as <widget-a> (https://github.com/example/widget.git)` | the duplicate kept, the token or userinfo in the key, the winner taken from argument order |
| `widget-a`, `mirror.git` (bare, `origin` without userinfo) | `https://github.com/example/widget.git` at `mirror.git` | | `duplicate-repo` skipping `widget-a` | a mirror and a clone of one remote counted twice |
| `scp`, `https` | `git@github.com:o/r.git`; `https://github.com/o/r.git` | | | the scp and HTTPS forms collapsed |
| `unparsed-a`, `unparsed-b` (`https:/user:TOKENVALUE@…`, `https//user:TOKENVALUE@…`) | `local:unparsed-a`, `local:unparsed-b`, remote `<unparsed-remote>` | | | `<unparsed-remote>` used as a key |
| `reset` (`remote.origin.url` is the widget URL with `TOKENVALUE`, then an empty value, then `https://github.com/example/reset.git`), `widget-a` | `https://github.com/example/reset.git`; `https://github.com/example/widget.git` | | none | the first URL kept although the empty value cleared it, which also makes `reset` a duplicate of `widget-a` |
| `bare.git` (`HEAD` → `trunk`, no `origin`), `team` | `…/api.git` (`main`); `…/web.git` (bare, `HEAD` → `trunk`); `local:bare`; `local:linked` (a worktree: `.git` is a file) | `team` holds the three members; `api-link`, a link to `api`, is `api` again; `notes/`, which holds a clone, `README.md` and `lost+found`, which nobody may read, are not members | none | a bare repo skipped or read as a group; a worktree missed; a walk deeper than one level; a link to a member counted as a second clone; an unreadable child reported as a failure |
| `outer` | `https://github.com/example/outer.git` only | | | the nested clone `outer/inner` added |
| `project` (`.git` holds `gitdir: ./.bare`; `.bare` is a bare clone with `HEAD` → `trunk`; worktree `project/main` beside it) | `https://github.com/example/project.git`: bare, named `project`, at `project`, branch `trunk` | | none | the layout read as "no work tree here" and failed, or as a group of `.bare` and `main`; the worktree added |
| `b/src`, `c/src-2` (empty), `a/src` | `local:one` in `src`; `local:two` in `src-3` | `src` (`a/src`), `src-2` (`c/src-2`), `src-3` (`b/src`) | | a suffix that collides with another group's own name |
| `team/api`, `widget-a` twice (once with a trailing `/`), `widget-link` (a link to `widget-a`), `team`, `lab`, `lab/empty` (no commits) | `api`, `web.git` and `linked` in `team`; `widget-a` once | `team`; `lab`, with no repo | no warning; one failure, `lab/empty` | one directory reached twice warned about, inspected twice (so `empty` fails twice), or dropped from its group |
| `file.txt`, `missing`, `lab/empty` (no commits), `broken` (`.git` file to a missing dir), `outer/stray` (empty `.git` dir), `bare.git/stray.git` (bad `HEAD`), `bare.git/stray-tree` (empty `.git` dir), `headless` (a bare clone without `HEAD`), `unfinished.git` (empty), `widget-a` | `widget-a` only | none | nine failures, one per path | a failure that stops the run; a broken repo, or a bare one git rejects, read as a group; git's answer for an enclosing repo taken as the path's own |

The default branch, from one call over the nine work trees (the bare rows come from the `bare.git`, `team` call above). A clone with upstream's remote-tracking refs is measured at them; only the rows with no `origin` fall back to a local branch or `HEAD` ([ADR 0009](../../docs/adr/0009-default-branch-as-upstream-last-fetched.md)):

| Repo | Refs | Branch | Head | Wrong implementation it catches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `widget-a` | `origin/HEAD` → `origin/main` | `main` | `main` | |
| `tracking` | `origin/HEAD` → `origin/trunk`; local `main`; local `trunk` one commit ahead of `origin/trunk` | `trunk` | `trunk` | `main` preferred to `origin/HEAD`; the local commit, which never landed, measured |
| `no-origin-head` | no `origin/HEAD`; `origin/main` fetched to `trunk`; local `main` at `main`, behind it | `main` | `trunk` | the local branch measured because `origin/HEAD` is missing |
| `origin-master` | no `origin/HEAD`; `origin/master` at `trunk` and no `origin/main`; local `main` at `main` | `master` | `trunk` | a local `main` preferred to upstream's `master` |
| `dangling-head` | `origin/HEAD` → `origin/master`, which does not exist; `origin/main`; local `master` at `main` | (failure) | (failure) | a dangling `origin/HEAD` skipped, so that `origin/main` or a local `master` upstream deleted is measured; the failure reads `origin/HEAD points at origin/master, which does not exist: …` |
| `main-first` | no `origin`; `main`, `master` (at `trunk`), `feature` checked out | `main` | `main` | `master` or `HEAD` preferred to `main` |
| `master-only` | no `origin`; `master` (at `main`), `feature` (at `trunk`) checked out | `master` | `main` | `HEAD` preferred to `master` |
| `current` | no `origin`; only `dev` (at `trunk`) | `dev` | `trunk` | no fallback to `HEAD` |
| `detached` | no `origin`; no branch; `HEAD` detached at `trunk` | `HEAD` | `trunk` | a detached `HEAD` treated as an error |
| `bare.git`, `team/web.git` | bare; `main` and `trunk`; `HEAD` → `trunk` | `trunk` | `trunk` | the work-tree rules applied to a bare repo |

The token check runs `Discover` over every path above with git's debug log on: the configs of `widget-a`, `unparsed-a` and `reset` hold `TOKENVALUE`, and the result (as JSON and as Go values) and the log do not. The clone-health bullets above run on `fixture.CloneHealth`: a complete clone, a `--depth 1` clone, a `--filter=blob:none` clone whose `origin` is the fake promisor, and complete clones marked partial by `extensions.partialClone`, by a promisor remote other than `origin`, and not partial by `remote.origin.promisor=false`.

## What fails CI

- **Oracles.** Any week or still-here oracle above changes. That includes Frank's 3 versus 2, Ivy's `prod_lines_added` 0, Jules's 0-line commit, Erin's rename insertion of 1, Ada's single mailmapped week row, and both Gina and Hank at `majority_files` 1.
- **Change oracles.** Any value in the change-oracle tables of either fixture changes. That includes Bob's move keeping 0 of 2, Ada's `durable@1` N of 2, Cara's absence from `durable@1`, `knowledge_loss@1` at 4/34, Lena eligible at exactly 10 clusters in both metrics, Omar not eligible at 9, S1 simplifying at exactly −20, S2 not simplifying at −16, Q1 untagged, M tagged through P2, and C1's 4 surviving lines credited to Pia (`surviving@1` 9), not to Copilot.
- **Regression guards.** A landing below a backdated first-parent commit goes missing, or that commit's own change counts for a landing; a rebased landing is chosen or dated by its author time, or credited to its committer; a revert that a `--no-ff` merge landed is not linked to the merge, or the merge's commits count in `durable@1` or `simplifying@1`, or the lines the revert restored leave `surviving@1`.
- **Classification.** `tests/test_service.py` is classified `prod`, or `bootstrap/cache/config.php` is blamed.
- **Discovery.** A duplicate remote is not skipped, a scrubbed URL contains userinfo, a bare repo is skipped, the SSH and HTTPS forms of one path are collapsed, or a work tree is measured at a local branch although its clone has upstream's.
- **Isolation.** A repo whose git directory was removed makes a sibling repo disappear, or the run exits 1 when the sibling succeeded.
- **Policy.** The policy hash is missing from the output, a user policy missing `[bots]` exits 0, or `--days 1` leaves `window.days` at 7.
- **Draft JSON.** The output omits `errors.blame` or `group_rollups` (until M1 supersedes the format).
- **Cache**, only if open decision #3 ships: a blame-cache miss on the second scan of the untouched fixture, or a hit after an amend without `gc`.
- **M3 web** (`TestWebEscaping`): a rendered page contains an email address, or the unescaped bytes `Frank & Sons`. The escaped text node `Frank &amp; Sons` is required. Pages are rendered with Go `html/template`. The 2026-10-07 rule against any `<script` element belonged to the single-file HTML design and is superseded.
- **Java** is never required in CI.

## To derive by hand before code (M1/M2)

Work out the expected values from the history above and write them into this file before writing the code that computes them. The implementation must never produce its own oracle.

- **Done for M1 (issue #3):** `durable@1` per landing and per person, `simplifying@1`, revert detection, AI-assisted tagging, `knowledge_loss@1` and `who_knows@1`.
